key_insight: The paper proposes a solved-volatility turbulence closure where the stochastic displacement field is computed alongside velocity, using Itô–Hencky kinematics and source-consistent momentum balance to make the closure mechanically and energetically self-consistent.
engineering_relevance: This framework could enable more physically grounded stochastic CFD closures for turbulence, especially where volume preservation, momentum sources, and finite-correlation effects matter.
method: Builds a one-channel Itô configuration map with local matrix-logarithm Hencky increments.
Derives pathwise isochoricity, quadratic-variation drift terms, and a momentum equation consistent with stochastic Reynolds transport.
Constructs a finite-correlation precursor with Green–Kubo-style covariance realization and index-one DAE structure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations and limit analyses rather than numerical validation; CFD validation and developed turbulent statistics are explicitly deferred to a later study.
watch_item: The closure is mathematically intricate and appears to require careful handling of constraints, covariance compatibility, and implementation of the index-one differential-algebraic system.
paper_title: Foundations of a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure: Itô--Hencky kinematics, source-consistent momentum and finite-correlation realisation
